lines.text: The Cathedral of the Seven holds ten thousand people. That morning, I think it held eleven.

The King on his throne. Mirelle beside him. Sabine and her children in purple, Prince Aurelio in gold. And in the middle of it all, on the very spot where Aldric once lit seven, stood the new Stone, white as milk.
First they measured the year's heirs. Five. Five. Five. Five. The court cheered every one of them, and nobody counted.
Lucan Varr, of Greyhollow. Who comes before the Stone by the old rite, with his sword, his seal... and his hound.
The cathedral laughed so hard the candles shook. A year ago, that laugh would have broken me. That morning, it was the sweetest sound I had ever heard. Nobody laughs at what they're afraid of.
Oswin's sword on my hip. Greyhollow's seal at my belt. And Ash beside me, padding down the aisle like a bridegroom.
Wren and Oswin gripped the gallery rail. Tamsin stood with the Measurers. Ilse was somewhere in the crowd, in her square spectacles, not breathing.
Your hand, Lord Lucan. I'll hold it there for you. The rite takes as long as it takes.
His fingers closed round my wrist, gentle as a nurse. He lowered my hand toward the Stone. And in the last instant before my skin touched it, I let go.
Everything went out of me, into Ash. All at once. Like a breath I'd been holding all my life.
The Stone touched my palm, and drank, and found nothing. It kept searching, pulling at me like a cold mouth. Vance's hand never moved. And I kept pouring, until my fingers were white with frost.
The Stone stayed dark. Not one ring. Not a flicker. Just milk-white glass, like the bottom of an empty cup.
Zero.
And no crack. Not in the Stone.
Behind me, under Ash's paws, there was a sound like a frozen lake giving way. A crack ran out across the cathedral floor. Across the very stone where Aldric had stood.
Nobody heard it. The whole cathedral was already laughing.
Zero. Well. Zero, then!
Sabine smiled behind her fan. Mirelle didn't laugh. She was looking at my hand, white with frost to the wrist. And Aurelio wasn't looking at me at all. He was looking at my dog.
Vance let go of my wrist, and smiled at me. Then he looked down at the crack under Ash's paws.
And smiled wider.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter seventy-nine, coming soon.
